keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Aeolian (Natural Minor) with aggressive, driving energy and blues-rock inflections
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: E minor is the relative minor of G major

mainProgression.description: The main riff is built on the E minor tonic using natural harmonics, palm-muted open E strings, and a galloping rhythm pattern rather than a traditional chord progression.

sectionProgressions.description: Iconic riff combining natural harmonics at the 12th fret with aggressive palm-muted open E galloping rhythm
Power chord verse progression anchored to the E minor tonic with movement to G and A for harmonic interest
Ascending power chord movement building from the submediant through subtonic to tonic resolution
Extended build using subdominant to submediant movement before resolving through D to E

harmonicFunction: E5 (i) - Tonic pedal tone forming the rhythmic and harmonic anchor of the song
G5 (III) - Major mediant providing contrast and lift from the minor tonic
A5 (IV) - Subdominant adding forward harmonic motion in the verse
C5 (VI) - Submediant opening the chorus with a broader harmonic perspective
D5 (VII) - Subtonic chord creating a strong pull back to the tonic E

techniques.name: Natural Harmonics Riff
techniques.description: The iconic opening riff using natural harmonics at the 12th fret of the low E string combined with aggressive open string attacks, creating the instantly recognizable Barracuda sound

notes: Natural harmonic at 12th fret of low E string: lightly touch string directly above 12th fret wire
Immediately release finger contact after picking to let the harmonic ring
Follow the harmonic with aggressive open E string palm-muted gallop
The harmonic should ring clearly at the same pitch as the 12th fret note (E)
Alternate between the clear harmonic ring and tight palm-muted attacks
The contrast between the bell-like harmonic and tight staccato picking is the signature sound
sequence: Lightly touch the 12th fret of the low E string (do not press down)
Pick the string with firm attack and immediately release the fretting finger
Let the harmonic ring for the specified duration
Immediately follow with palm-muted open E string gallop pattern
Repeat the harmonic-to-gallop pattern for the riff cycle
Maintain strict timing at 136 BPM throughout
tips: Practice the 12th fret harmonic in isolation until it rings clearly every time
The picking hand attack must be confident - weak picking will not produce the harmonic
Keep the fretting finger light - just touching, not pressing
The transition from harmonic to palm mute must be instantaneous
Use the bridge pickup for maximum harmonic clarity and attack

techniques.name: Galloping Rhythm
techniques.description: A driving palm-muted rhythm pattern with a galloping triplet feel (eighth-sixteenth-sixteenth or dotted-eighth-sixteenth grouping) that propels the song forward with relentless energy

notes: The gallop pattern: strong downstroke followed by two quick alternate strokes
Rhythmic pattern: DUM-da-da DUM-da-da (accented on the first beat of each group)
All notes played on the palm-muted low E string for tight, percussive attack
Palm pressure should be firm for maximum staccato effect
At 136 BPM, this requires significant right-hand stamina and control
The pattern is similar to Iron Maiden's gallop but at a faster tempo
sequence: Position palm edge firmly on strings near the bridge
Play a strong downstroke on the low E string
Follow with two quick alternate strokes (up-down or down-up depending on preference)
Accent the first note of each group heavily
Maintain the galloping pattern for extended periods
Transition smoothly from gallop to power chord sections
tips: Build stamina gradually - this pattern at 136 BPM is physically demanding
Keep the picking wrist relaxed to avoid fatigue and injury
Start at 80 BPM and increase by 5 BPM increments
The palm mute should be tight and consistent - no ringing notes in the gallop
Practice for short bursts at first, gradually increasing duration

techniques.name: Power Chord Transitions
techniques.description: Fast power chord changes through the verse and chorus sections, requiring quick position shifts along the neck while maintaining the driving rhythm

notes: E5: 0-2-2-X-X-X (open position)
G5: 3-5-5-X-X-X (3rd fret root)
A5: 5-7-7-X-X-X (5th fret root) or X-0-2-2-X-X (open position)
C5: 8-10-10-X-X-X (8th fret root) or X-3-5-5-X-X (3rd fret A string root)
D5: 10-12-12-X-X-X (10th fret root) or X-5-7-7-X-X (5th fret A string root)
Quick shifts between positions require efficient left-hand movement
Mute unused strings with the underside of the fretting fingers
sequence: Play E5 in open position with full downstroke attack
Shift quickly to G5 at 3rd fret for the verse movement
Move to A5 at 5th fret maintaining rhythm
For the chorus: ascend from C5 through D5 to E5
tips: Pre-visualize where each chord shape sits on the neck before the song starts
Minimize finger movement between chord positions
Keep the fretting hand close to the fretboard during transitions
Practice the chord order slowly until the position shifts feel automatic
details.progression: E5 - G5 - A5 - E5 (verse) / C5 - D5 - E5 (chorus)

sections.name: Intro / Main Riff
sections.description: The instantly recognizable intro combining 12th fret harmonics with aggressive palm-muted galloping rhythm on the open E string
notes: Natural harmonics at 12th fret must ring clearly above the palm-muted gallop
The palm-muted low E string should be tight and percussive
Keep strict time at 136 BPM - the gallop drives the song's energy
Bridge pickup recommended for harmonic clarity and aggressive attack

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: Driving verse section with power chord movement supporting Ann Wilson's powerful vocal delivery
notes: Aggressive downstroke power chords with consistent attack
The i-III-IV-i movement provides harmonic interest under the vocal melody
Maintain the driving energy established by the intro riff
Quick position shifts between E5, G5, and A5 require practiced transitions

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: Ascending power chord chorus section with the signature the signature vocal hook and building intensity
notes: Ascending progression creates a sense of building power and resolution
Full-volume power chord attack for maximum impact
The C5-D5-E5 movement (VI-VII-i) resolves strongly to the tonic
Emphasize the final E5 arrival as the peak of each chorus phrase

sections.name: Guitar Solo
sections.technique: Lead Guitar in E Minor Pentatonic
sections.description: Nancy Wilson's fiery guitar solo using E minor pentatonic and blues scale patterns over the verse chord progression
notes: Solo is based in the E minor pentatonic box pattern at the 12th fret
Uses aggressive bending, vibrato, and fast hammer-on/pull-off runs
The rhythm section maintains the verse progression beneath the solo
Nancy Wilson's lead style combines blues-rock vocabulary with hard rock intensity

sections.name: Outro
sections.description: Return of the iconic harmonic riff building to a climactic ending with full band intensity
notes: Return of the main riff with maximum intensity
The galloping rhythm drives to the final climax
Song builds to its loudest point in the final measures
Concludes with a powerful E5 resolution

guitar.recommended: Gibson Les Paul or similar humbucker-equipped guitar
guitar.pickup: Bridge humbucker for maximum attack, harmonic clarity, and aggressive tone

amp.recommended: Marshall JMP or JCM800 Super Lead

settings.presence: 7-8 (cut and bite for the riff's attack)

effects.distortion: Natural amp overdrive preferred. Optional boost pedal (Ibanez TS-9 or similar) for solo sections.
effects.delay: None for the main riff. Optional subtle delay on solo sections.
effects.reverb: Dry to minimal - the riff requires tightness and precision
effects.other: Noise gate recommended for clean palm-mute releases. No modulation effects.

beginner.focus: Learn the basic power chord shapes and simplified rhythm without the gallop
steps: Master E5, G5, A5, C5, and D5 power chord shapes
Learn the verse and chorus chord progressions with simple downstrokes
Practice basic palm muting technique on the low E string
Get familiar with the song structure and chord order

intermediate.focus: Develop the galloping rhythm pattern and natural harmonic technique
steps: Practice the galloping rhythm pattern slowly (80 BPM) on muted strings
Learn to produce consistent 12th fret natural harmonics
Combine harmonics with the palm-muted gallop at slow tempo
Gradually increase tempo toward 136 BPM while maintaining precision

advanced.focus: Play the complete song at tempo with authentic tone and lead guitar elements
steps: Play the full riff at 136 BPM with clean harmonics and tight gallop
Add the guitar solo using E minor pentatonic patterns
Work on stamina for sustaining the gallop through the entire song
Achieve the authentic Nancy Wilson tone with proper amp and pickup settings

commonMistakes: Harmonics not ringing clearly due to incorrect finger placement or weak picking
Galloping rhythm becoming uneven or losing the accent pattern at tempo
Palm mute too loose, causing the gallop to sound muddy instead of tight
Right-hand fatigue causing inconsistency during extended galloping sections
practiceRoutine: Warm up with natural harmonics on all strings at the 12th, 7th, and 5th frets for 5 minutes
Practice the galloping pattern on muted strings, starting at 80 BPM for 5 minutes
Combine harmonics with gallop at 80 BPM, increasing by 5 BPM every few minutes
Work on the verse power chord transitions (E5-G5-A5-E5) with galloping rhythm
Play through complete song sections at maximum comfortable tempo
focusAreas: Clean, ringing natural harmonics with confident picking attack
Consistent galloping rhythm at 136 BPM without fatigue
Tight palm muting for percussive precision
metronomeWork: Start the gallop pattern at 80 BPM and increase by 5 BPM per practice session
Practice harmonic-to-gallop transitions with metronome at incrementally increasing tempos
Work on the full riff at 100 BPM, then 120 BPM, then target 136 BPM
Use a metronome at half tempo (68 BPM on half notes) to internalize the larger groove
